newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon announces new foray into capital markets.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon announces new foray into capital markets.

text.p: Lebanon said on Wednesday it was preparing a $100 million eurobond to help finance the reconstruction of its war-damaged electricity network -- the country's fourth foray into international capital markets.

"The finance ministry was instructed to prepare for a $100 million eurobond issue for (state-run utility) Electricite du Liban," Information Minister Farid Makari told reporters after a cabinet session.

Billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri's government has already borrowed a total of $800 million in three Eurobond issues since September 1994, to finance its multi-billion dollar programme to reconstruct Lebanon from the 1975-90 civil war.
Makari did not give a date for the new eurobond issue but he said the World Bank would be guarantor of the principal and the Lebanese government would guarantee the interest.
The plan was within the context of a draft law sent earlier to parliament allowing the government to borrow $365 million for rebuilding electricity stations and lines, Makari added.

The Lebanese government in May issued a $100 million addition to a $300 million 9.125 percent eurobond issued in July 1995. The proceeds of the four-year issues, both lead managed by Paribas Capital Markets, were to be used to rebuild the infrastructure of villages damaged in the war.
Beirut's first highly successful venture into international capital markets was a $400-million three year eurobond, at 10.125 percent, in September 1994.
The first two issues were oversubscribed -- the first one drew offers of $792 million and some Beirut bankers said then that the coupon on it was too high.

Makari also said that the ministry of electricity plans to send a delegation for talks with the World Bank for a $65-million loan to finance the rebuilding of the electricity networks and major sub-stations in south and east Lebanon.

He said the government's reconstruction agency, the Council for Developement and Reconstruction, was also delegated to sign a $20.08 million loan deal with Paribas Capital Markets and another loan deal for $4.7 million with Beirut's Banque Saradar to help finance the construction of power lines.
